title: Accelerating ab initio melting property calculations with machine learning: application to the high entropy alloy TaVCrW

recollection.starting_material: Guess: An equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy TaVCrW forming a BCC solid-solution at high temperature.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Training a machine-learning interatomic potential (e.g., SNAP/MTP/NequIP-class) on ab initio (DFT) data for solid and liquid configurations with active learning, then using large-scale MD (two-phase solid–liquid coexistence and/or thermodynamic integration) to compute the melting temperature and melting curve; validated by smaller-cell ab initio MD.
recollection.structure: Guess: A BCC solid solution exhibiting limited chemical short-range order at high T, and a chemically well-mixed metallic liquid; no phase separation observed near melting.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The ML potential reproduces ab initio energetics and forces, enabling long-time, large-cell coexistence simulations to equilibrate solid–liquid interfaces and determine Tm and latent heat; free-energy matching and the Clapeyron relation provide dTm/dP; explicit treatment of configurational disorder and anharmonicity improves accuracy over harmonic approximations.
recollection.results: Guess: Ambient-pressure melting temperature Tm on the order of 3000–3300 K for TaVCrW; latent heat of fusion ~0.35–0.6 eV/atom; solid–liquid density contrast ~3–6%; entropy of fusion ~1.5–2.5 kB/atom; slope of melting curve dTm/dP ~15–30 K/GPa; ab initio validation within ~50–100 K of the ML-based values.

score.note: The recollection generically identifies an ML interatomic potential and the BCC TaVCrW alloy, but misses the specific MTP-for-liquid plus FEP-replacing-TI workflow. It does not recall the key phase-space fidelity/training error, rapid FEP convergence from low MTP–DFT energy-difference variance, electronic Gibbs contribution, or SRO stabilization. Its coexistence/Clapeyron mechanism and all numerical estimates are unsupported and omit the reported 80% savings, 193/160 K CALPHAD offsets, 48/57 K electronic shifts, and 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization.
